note: Fixtures are described in `fixture` and not shipped, so build each one as a small folder before the run. Evals 0 to 2 test what the rules change, and their assertions are checked on the edited files and the transcript. Eval 3 is a near-miss: a derivation with no statement of a result, which the writing-math skill covers.

evals.name: restructure-lasso-theorem
evals.prompt: clean up the statement of theorem 2 in theory/lasso-rate.tex
evals.fixture: paper/ on high-dimensional regression, with main.tex, sections/10-introduction.tex and theory/lasso-rate.tex. The introduction says the paper's contribution is to show how the restricted eigenvalue constant drives the lasso error. sections/20-setup.tex defines the design matrix X with n rows and p columns, the true coefficient vector \beta^*, its support S with s = |S|, and the noise vector. Theorem 2 reads, in one paragraph: 'Let \hat\beta be the lasso estimate with \lambda = 2\sigma\sqrt{2\log(2p)/n}, where the noise is sub-Gaussian with parameter \sigma. Suppose the columns of X are normalized, \beta^* is s-sparse, and X satisfies the restricted eigenvalue condition over S with constant \kappa > 0. Then \|\hat\beta - \beta^*\|_2 \le C \sigma \sqrt{s \log p / n} / \kappa with probability at least 1 - 1/p (in fact C = 3 works, and sub-Gaussian noise can be relaxed to finite fourth moments at the cost of a log factor). If, in addition, \min_{j \in S} |\beta^*_j| > 2 C \sigma \sqrt{s \log p / n} / \kappa, the lasso recovers S.' The proof in the same file uses every condition in the statement.
evals.expected_output: Moves the sub-Gaussian noise condition out of the Let part, so that the Let part only names the lasso estimate and its tuning parameter. Puts the regularity conditions, such as sub-Gaussian noise and normalized columns, inline in a Suppose that part. Treats the restricted eigenvalue condition as substantive, given the introduction, and puts it in an If part. Displays the error bound in the Then part. Says what the constant C depends on, or states its value, and keeps the probability statement. Moves the remarks about C = 3 and about fourth moments to a paragraph after the statement. Turns the support-recovery sentence into a corollary that starts 'Assume the conditions of' Theorem 2, cited with \cref.
assertions: The Let part of the rewritten theorem imposes no condition on the noise
Sub-Gaussian noise and normalized columns are in a Suppose that part, written inline and not as display equations
The restricted eigenvalue condition is in an If part
The error bound on \|\hat\beta - \beta^*\|_2 is a display equation
The statement says what C depends on or gives its value, and keeps the probability at least 1 - 1/p
The remarks about C = 3 and about finite fourth moments are not inside the theorem environment and appear in a paragraph after it
The support-recovery claim is a separate corollary that starts with 'Assume the conditions of' and cites Theorem 2 with \cref, and no sentence starts with 'If, in addition'

evals.name: lemma-in-quarto-note
evals.prompt: in notes/sample-split.qmd, state the lemma we used to kill the empirical process term, right before the step that uses it
evals.fixture: a Quarto project whose notes/sample-split.qmd holds a derivation in Quarto's $...$ math. It defines the empirical measure P_n of n observations, the true distribution P, a fixed function f_0 and an estimate \hat f that is fit on a second sample independent of the n observations. One step of the derivation says '(P_n - P)(\hat f - f_0) = o_P(n^{-1/2}) by sample splitting and Chebyshev' with no stated lemma. The note has no .tex file and no lemma environments.
evals.expected_output: Writes the lemma in Quarto syntax, before the step that uses it. The Let part names \hat f as an estimate fit on an independent sample, with no further condition on it. A Suppose that part states boundedness or a second-moment condition inline. The If part states \|\hat f - f_0\|_{L_2(P)} = o_P(1). The Then part displays (P_n - P)(\hat f - f_0) = o_P(n^{-1/2}) and says that the order is in probability as n grows. The statement has no symbol that only the proof uses, such as a conditional variance, and no commentary. The derivation step then cites the lemma.
assertions: The lemma is written in Quarto math syntax in notes/sample-split.qmd and placed before the step that uses it
The lemma has a Let part, a Suppose that or If part, and a Then part, in that order
The L2 consistency of \hat f is in the If part, not in the Let part
The conclusion (P_n - P)(\hat f - f_0) = o_P(n^{-1/2}) is a display equation
The statement defines no symbol that only the proof uses
The step of the derivation that used 'sample splitting and Chebyshev' now refers to the lemma

evals.name: corollary-not-in-addition
evals.prompt: add to theorem 1 that the estimator is efficient when the outcome regression is correctly specified
evals.fixture: paper/ on a regression-adjusted estimator in randomized trials. theory/adjusted-normal.tex holds Theorem 1, with \label{thm:adjusted-normal}, which states asymptotic normality of the estimator \hat\tau with an asymptotic variance V given in a display, under bounded outcomes and a known randomization probability. sections/20-setup.tex defines the efficiency bound V^* in a labelled equation, eq:bound.
evals.expected_output: Leaves the statement of Theorem 1 unchanged. Adds a corollary after it, in its own file or in the same theory file as the paper's layout requires, that starts 'Assume the conditions of \cref{thm:adjusted-normal} hold.', then says 'If' the outcome regression is correctly specified, 'then' V = V^*, with V = V^* displayed. Adds a short paragraph after the corollary that says what it means.
assertions: The statement of Theorem 1 is unchanged
No sentence in the new text starts with 'If, in addition'
A new corollary starts with 'Assume the conditions of' and cites Theorem 1 with \cref
The correct specification of the outcome regression is in the corollary's If part
The conclusion that the asymptotic variance equals the efficiency bound is a display equation

evals.name: near-miss-derivation
evals.prompt: in notes/allocation.tex, work out the treated fraction that minimizes the variance of the difference in means
evals.fixture: notes/allocation.tex, a standalone note whose first line is the mode line % writing-math: note, design of experiments. It defines n units, the treated fraction p, the outcome standard deviations \sigma_1 and \sigma_0 in the treated and the control arm, and the difference-in-means estimator \hat\tau. It has no theorem, lemma or proposition.
evals.expected_output: Judges the skill not to apply, since the task is a derivation with no statement of a result. Follows writing-math in note mode. Does not invoke writing-proofs.
assertions: Does not invoke the writing-proofs skill
